book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 53 · Hazardous Materials Incidents
title: Hazmat Scenes: Zones, Decon and Care After Decon

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already size up every scene, wear PPE, call for help and give high-flow oxygen. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Recognize a hazmat scene and identify the substance from a safe distance
  2. Know the zones, PPE levels and decon, and where you fit
  3. Care after decon: what the PCP adds, what's not on the BC exam

Textbook: Chapter 53, PDF pages 4341–4383
slides.say: Welcome to class. Today's topic is hazardous materials, or hazmat. As EMRs, you already size up every scene, wear protective equipment, call for help and give high-flow oxygen. Those habits matter even more here, because a hazmat scene can kill you. As a PCP, you may also receive poisoned patients after decontamination, choose the BC protocol, decide about CPAP and an IV, and monitor the hazmat team. Today we cover three things: recognizing a hazmat scene and identifying the substance safely; zones, protective equipment and decon; and what the PCP adds after decon, including what's not on the BC licensing exam.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来上课。今天讲危险品，也叫 hazmat。你们作为 EMR，早就会评估每个现场、穿戴防护装备、呼叫支援、给高流量氧。这些习惯在这里更重要，因为危险品现场能要你的命。作为 PCP，你还可能在洗消后接收中毒病人、选择 BC 流程、决定要不要用 CPAP 和开静脉，并为危险品队员做监测。今天讲三件事：识别危险品现场，并安全地辨认物质；分区、防护装备和洗消；以及洗消后 PCP 多做什么，包括哪些不在 BC 执照考试范围内。

slides.title: Spot it, then stay back
slides.body:
• Dispatch mentions a chemical? Treat it as hazmat
  • Tankers, rail cars, plants, farms, drug labs: be suspicious
  • Several people down at once → suspect a hazardous material
  • Cloud, leak, strong odour: if you smell it, you're exposed
  • No placard ≠ safe: small loads and mixtures can fool you

First on scene: stop far back, upwind and uphill. Isolate, deny entry, call for help.
slides.say: Scene safety is an EMR habit, and hazmat calls test it hardest. If dispatch mentions a chemical, treat the call as hazmat. Be suspicious of tankers, rail cars, plants, farms and drug labs. Several people collapsed or short of breath at once? Suspect a hazardous material, not bad luck. Watch for clouds, leaks and strong smells, but never use your nose as a detector: if you can smell it, you're already exposed. No placard doesn't mean safe; small loads may not need one, and mixtures can turn toxic. First on scene, stop far back, upwind and uphill, isolate the area, keep people out, and call for help.
slides.sayZh: 现场安全是 EMR 的老习惯，而危险品呼叫对它的考验最大。调度一提到化学品，就按危险品事件处理。对罐车、铁路货车、工厂、农场和制毒窝点要保持警惕。好几个人同时倒下或喘不上气？要怀疑是危险品，而不是运气不好。注意烟雾、泄漏和强烈气味，但千万别拿鼻子当探测器：闻得到，说明你已经暴露了。没有标牌不代表安全：少量货物可能不需要挂标牌，混合物也可能变得有毒。第一个到场时，停在远处、上风、高处，隔离现场、禁止他人进入、呼叫支援。

slides.title: Identify it from a distance
slides.body:
• Placard → 4-digit UN number → look it up in the ERG
  • ERG: hazards, placard meanings, isolation distances
  • Truck: bill of lading in the cab; train: waybill with the conductor
  • Fixed site: ask for the SDS and read all of it
  • CANUTEC, 24 h: 613-996-6666 (collect) or *666 by cell

Use binoculars and the thumb rule: if your thumb at arm's length can't cover the scene, you're too close.
slides.say: Identifying the substance is one of the most valuable things you can do, without taking risks. Placards carry a four-digit UN number. Look it up in Transport Canada's Emergency Response Guidebook, the ERG, which every emergency vehicle should carry; it gives the hazards and how far back to keep people. Truck drivers carry a bill of lading; train conductors carry a waybill. At a factory, ask for the safety data sheets, or SDS, and read them fully. CANUTEC, Transport Canada's hazmat advice line, answers day and night. Use binoculars: if your thumb at arm's length can't cover the whole scene, you're too close.
slides.sayZh: 辨认出是什么物质，是你能做的最有价值的事之一，前提是不冒风险。标牌上有四位数的 UN 编号，拿它去查加拿大交通部的《应急响应指南》，也就是 ERG；每辆应急车都应该带一本，里面写着危害是什么、要让人员退开多远。卡车司机带着提单，列车长带着运单。在工厂，要索取安全数据表，也就是 SDS，并且读完整份。CANUTEC 是加拿大交通部的危险品咨询热线，昼夜都有人接听。用望远镜：手臂伸直竖起拇指，如果盖不住整个现场，说明你离得太近了。

slides.title: Hot, warm and cold zones
slides.body:
Hotthe contaminated areatrained entry team in PPE only
Warmaround the hot zone; decon corridorhazmat specialists only
Coldcommand and supportwhere you triage and treat

Training: Awareness = recognize, isolate, call · Operations = cold-zone care · Technician = warm-zone care
slides.say: The hazmat team sets up three zones. The hot zone is the contaminated area: only trained rescuers in the right protective equipment go in. The warm zone surrounds it and usually holds the decon corridor; it's for hazmat specialists too. The cold zone is the outer buffer with command and support, where paramedics normally triage and treat. Your training decides your zone. Every paramedic needs Awareness level: recognize, isolate, call for help. Operations level treats cold-zone patients with no real risk of secondary contamination, meaning passing the chemical on to others. Only Technicians work in the warm zone. In short: hot is off limits, warm is for decon, cold is yours.
slides.sayZh: 危险品队会划出三个区。热区是污染区，只有受过训练、穿着合适防护装备的救援者才能进。温区环绕热区，通常设有洗消通道，同样只有危险品专业人员能进。冷区是最外层的缓冲区，有指挥和支援，护理人员通常在这里分诊和救治。你的培训等级决定你能进哪个区。每个护理人员都需要认知级：识别、隔离、呼叫支援。操作级可以在冷区救治没有明显二次污染风险的病人，二次污染就是把化学品再传给别人。只有技术员级才能在温区工作。一句话：热区进不去，温区做洗消，冷区才是你的。

slides.q: You're first on scene at a tanker rollover. A yellow cloud is drifting from the tank, and the driver is sitting in the ditch, coughing. What do you do first?
options: Put on gloves and a surgical mask and drag the driver to your ambulance
Stop far back, upwind and uphill; isolate, deny entry and call for hazmat
Drive closer so you can read the placard's UN number
Park downwind and wait for the cloud to clear
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. You're first on scene at a tanker rollover. A yellow cloud is drifting from the tank, and the driver is sitting in the ditch, coughing. What do you do first? A, put on gloves and a surgical mask and drag the driver to your ambulance. B, stop far back, upwind and uphill, then isolate, deny entry and call for hazmat. C, drive closer so you can read the placard's UN number. D, park downwind and wait for the cloud to clear. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。你第一个到达一起罐车侧翻现场，罐体飘出一团黄色烟雾，司机坐在路边沟里咳嗽。你首先做什么？A，戴上手套和外科口罩，把司机拖到救护车上；B，停在远处、上风、高处，然后隔离、禁止进入、呼叫危险品队；C，开近一点，好看清标牌上的 UN 编号；D，停在下风处，等烟雾散去。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. First on scene, protect yourself, isolate the area, keep people out and call for resources. Leaving the driver feels wrong, but trained rescuers in proper protection will bring him to the cold zone, where you treat him. A makes you a second patient: gloves and a surgical mask don't stop a toxic gas. C is wrong because if you can read a placard with the naked eye, you may already be too close. D puts you downwind, where the gas is going.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。第一个到场，要先保护自己、隔离现场、禁止他人进入、呼叫资源。丢下司机感觉不对，但穿着合适防护的受训救援者会把他带到冷区，你在那里救治他。A 会让你变成第二个病人：手套和外科口罩挡不住有毒气体。C 错在如果肉眼就能看清标牌，你可能已经太近了。D 让你站在下风处，正是毒气飘去的方向。

slides.title: PPE levels A to D
slides.body:
LevelWhat it isWho wears it
Afully sealed suit, SCBA insideentry team, worst hazards
Btop breathing protection, SCBA outsidedecon team
Csplash protection + filter respiratorED receivers, perimeter police
Dno respirator; dust mask at mostcold-zone support

Toxicity runs 0–4; an ambulance is equipped for level 0 only. Not dressed for it? Stay out.
slides.say: Hazmat teams use four levels of protective equipment, A to D. Level A is a fully sealed, gas-tight suit with the self-contained breathing apparatus, or SCBA, inside; it protects the most, but it's like a sauna. Level B has the same high breathing protection, with the air supply outside the suit; decon teams often wear it. Level C protects against a known substance, with a respirator filter matched to that chemical; hospital staff receiving patients might wear it. Level D is for cold-zone support only, with no real breathing protection. Most ambulances carry none of these and are ready only for toxicity level zero. Not dressed for it? Stay out.
slides.sayZh: 危险品队用四个等级的防护装备，A 到 D 级。A 级是全封闭、气密的防护服，自给式呼吸器，也就是 SCBA，穿在里面；防护最高，但穿着像在桑拿房里。B 级的呼吸防护同样高，但气源在防护服外面，洗消人员常穿。C 级针对已知物质，呼吸器的滤罐要与该化学品对应；接收病人的医院人员可能会穿。D 级只用于冷区支援，基本没有呼吸防护。大多数救护车一套都不带，只能应对毒性 0 级。没穿对装备？那就别进去。

slides.title: Emergency decon, step by step
slides.body:
1. Protect yourself: splash suit, eyes, HEPA mask, double gloves
  2. Undress: removes 80–90% of contamination; bag it all
  3. Brush off any powder first
  4. Flush: lots of water, unless it reacts with water
  5. Rinse armpits, fingers, toes, groin, scalp, buttocks
  6. Dry and warm; you start triage at the exit

Water dilution is the main method. Never neutralize on skin: the reaction makes heat.
slides.say: Decon has two goals: lower the dose reaching the patient, and stop secondary contamination of rescuers and hospital staff. When patients need rapid emergency decon, follow this order. First, protect yourself: a splash suit or turnout gear, eye protection, a high-efficiency mask, and at least two pairs of gloves, ideally nitrile. Second, have patients undress and bag everything; removing clothing alone takes off eighty to ninety percent of the contamination. Third, brush off powder. Fourth, flush with lots of water, unless the chemical reacts with water, including armpits, fingers, toes, groin, scalp and buttocks. Never try to neutralize a chemical on skin; the reaction makes heat. At the exit, have blankets ready, because children and older adults chill fast. That's where you start triage.
slides.sayZh: 洗消有两个目的：减少到达病人身上的剂量，以及防止救援者和医院人员被二次污染。病人需要紧急洗消时，按这个顺序。第一，保护好自己：穿防溅服或消防战斗服，戴护目镜和高效过滤口罩，至少戴两层手套，最好是丁腈手套。第二，让病人脱衣，所有东西装袋；单是脱掉衣服就能去掉百分之八十到九十的污染。第三，扫掉粉末。第四，用大量清水冲洗，除非该化学品遇水会反应；腋下、手指、脚趾、腹股沟、头皮和臀部都要冲到。千万别在皮肤上用化学品中和，反应会放热。出口处备好毯子，因为小孩和老人很快就会失温。你就在那里开始分诊。

slides.title: Receiving the patient after decon
slides.body:
• Assume not fully clean: wear your PPE
  • Get the full story: substance, how exposed, what decon was done
  • Still giving off fumes? Not ready to transport
  • Prep the truck: mattress off, supplies out, disposables
  • Double wrap: sheet around the patient → backboard → stretcher
  • Call the hospital early; it may decon again first
slides.say: Now the patient reaches you in the cold zone. Assume they aren't fully clean, because no patient ever is, and wear protective equipment. Get a full report: the substance, how the patient was exposed, and what decon and treatment were done. If the patient is still giving off fumes, decon isn't good enough; don't transport yet. Prepare the ambulance: mattress off the stretcher, supplies out, disposable equipment in. Don't waste time lining it with plastic; double wrap the patient instead, in a sheet, on a backboard, on the stretcher. Call the hospital early, because some will decon the patient again before letting you in.
slides.sayZh: 现在病人到了冷区，交给你。要假定他没有完全洗干净，因为没有任何病人能洗得完全干净，所以要穿好防护装备。拿到完整的交接：是什么物质、病人怎么接触到的、做了哪些洗消和处置。如果病人身上还在释放烟气，说明洗消不够，先别转运。准备救护车：撤掉担架床垫、搬出车内物品、改用一次性器材。别浪费时间给车厢铺塑料膜，改用双层包裹：用床单裹住病人，放到长背板上，再放上担架。尽早通知医院，因为有些医院会先给病人再洗消一遍，才让你进去。

slides.title: Toxic exposures after decon
slides.body:
AgentLook forKey point
Acids, alkalisskin, eye, airway burnsalkalis need longer flushing
Solventswet lungs, dysrhythmias, seizureskeep off-gassing
Chlorine, ammoniacough, chokingfresh air; clothes off
PesticidesSLUDGE, heavy secretionsvomit can contaminate you
CO, cyanidecells can't get or use O₂CO: high-flow O₂ whatever the SpO₂
slides.say: Here are the exposures you'll meet most. Acids and alkalis burn skin, eyes and, if inhaled, the airway and lungs; alkalis form a soapy layer, so they need longer flushing. Solvents, like paint thinner, can fill the lungs with fluid quickly, and long skin contact can cause rhythm problems and seizures. Chlorine and ammonia cause coughing and choking: fresh air, and remove clothing to release trapped gas. Organophosphate and carbamate pesticides cause SLUDGE: salivation, tears, urination, diarrhea, stomach upset and vomiting, plus heavy lung secretions; beware the vomit. Cyanide, most often from fire smoke, stops cells using oxygen. For carbon monoxide, give high-flow oxygen whatever the oximeter says.
slides.sayZh: 这些是你最常遇到的暴露。酸和碱会烧伤皮肤、眼睛；如果吸入，还会烧伤气道和肺；碱会形成一层皂样物，所以需要冲洗更久。溶剂，比如油漆稀释剂，可以很快让肺里积液；皮肤长时间接触还会导致心律问题和抽搐。氯气和氨会引起咳嗽和窒息感：呼吸新鲜空气，并脱掉衣服放出滞留的气体。有机磷和氨基甲酸酯类农药会引起 SLUDGE：流涎、流泪、排尿、腹泻、胃肠不适和呕吐，再加上大量肺分泌物；小心呕吐物。氰化物最常来自火灾烟雾，会让细胞无法利用氧。一氧化碳则不管血氧仪读数多少，都要给高流量氧。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: after decon
slides.body:
No BC hazmat protocol: use Oxygen Administration, CHF/Pulmonary Edema (indication: exposure to toxins) and Burn Management.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • CO or smoke: non-rebreather, high-flow O₂
  • Toxic lungs: upright, legs down, at rest, warm
  • O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Assist ventilations if LOC altered or SpO₂ < 94%
  • Burns: calculate BSA; sterile, nonstick dry dressing

PCP adds

  • Consider CPAP on scene if criteria are met
  • BVM needed? PEEP valve, start at 5 cmH₂O
  • Burns: IV if indicated
  • Hypotensive burn patient: 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
slides.say: BC has no hazmat protocol, so after decon you use the ones that fit. The oxygen guideline calls for a non-rebreather and high-flow oxygen for carbon monoxide and smoke. For chemical lung injury, the CHF or Pulmonary Edema protocol lists exposure to toxins as an indication. Every licence level sits the patient up with legs down, at rest and warm, gives oxygen to ninety-four percent or higher, and assists ventilations if consciousness is altered or the saturation is below ninety-four. Burns follow the burn protocol. The PCP adds CPAP if the criteria are met, a PEEP valve starting at five when bagging, and for burns, an IV if indicated, with twenty millilitres per kilogram, up to two litres, for hypotension.
slides.sayZh: BC 没有危险品流程，所以洗消后你要用适用的几个流程。给氧指南规定：一氧化碳中毒和吸入烟雾，用非重复呼吸面罩给高流量氧。化学性肺损伤可以用充血性心衰或肺水肿流程，它把「接触毒物」列为适应症之一。所有执照等级都要让病人坐直、双腿下垂、保持休息和保暖，给氧使血氧达到九十四或以上；如果意识改变或血氧低于九十四，就辅助通气。烧伤按烧伤流程处理。PCP 另外可以：符合标准时用 CPAP；用球囊面罩通气时加 PEEP 阀，从五开始；烧伤有指征时开静脉，低血压时按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升补液。

slides.q: After emergency decon, a farm worker exposed to an organophosphate is drooling, vomiting and wheezing, with heavy secretions. SpO₂ is 89% on oxygen. As the PCP, what is the best plan?
options: Apply CPAP right away to raise his saturation
Give atropine to dry up the secretions
Protect yourself, suction, high-flow O₂, assist ventilations, transport
Start an IV at the corridor exit before anything else
slides.say: Let's try a PCP decision. After emergency decon, a farm worker exposed to an organophosphate is drooling, vomiting and wheezing, with heavy secretions. His saturation is eighty-nine percent on oxygen. As the PCP, what is the best plan? A, apply CPAP right away to raise his saturation. B, give atropine to dry up the secretions. C, protect yourself, suction, give high-flow oxygen, assist ventilations, and transport. D, start an IV at the corridor exit before anything else. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。紧急洗消后，一名接触了有机磷的农场工人流口水、呕吐、喘鸣，肺分泌物很多，吸氧状态下血氧八十九。作为 PCP，最好的方案是什么？A，马上上 CPAP 提高血氧；B，给阿托品减少分泌物；C，做好自我防护，吸引，高流量给氧，辅助通气，转运；D，先在通道出口开静脉，其他的之后再说。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. He can still contaminate you, especially through vomit, so protect yourself, then suction, give high-flow oxygen, and assist ventilations because his saturation is below ninety-four. A is wrong: BC lists vomiting as a contraindication to CPAP. B is wrong: atropine is in the book, but not on the BC licensing exam. D puts a line ahead of the airway, and the book warns that an IV in a contaminated patient lets the chemical bypass the skin.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。他仍可能污染你，尤其是通过呕吐物，所以先防护好自己，再吸引、给高流量氧，并因为血氧低于九十四而辅助通气。A 错：BC 把呕吐列为 CPAP 的禁忌症。B 错：阿托品书里有，但不在 BC 执照考试范围内。D 把开静脉排在气道前面，而且书中提醒，在受污染的病人身上开静脉，会让化学品绕过皮肤屏障。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Your IV is a new door: it can let the chemical bypass the skin
  • Contaminated patient? Keep invasive steps minimal; weigh the risk
  • CPAP: not with vomiting, decreased LOC or systolic < 90
  • CO: the oximeter can look normal; treat the patient
  • Solvents keep off-gassing in a closed ambulance
  • Effects can be delayed: document scene, hazmat info, changes
slides.say: Here's what's new for you as a PCP. As an EMR you never put a needle in a patient. Now you can, and in a contaminated patient an IV is a new door that lets the chemical bypass the skin. The book says keep invasive procedures to a minimum and weigh risk against benefit, so finish decon first. BC says no CPAP with vomiting, a decreased level of consciousness, or a systolic under ninety, and poisoned patients often vomit or get drowsy. With carbon monoxide, treat the patient, not the oximeter. Solvents can off-gas in your closed ambulance. And effects can appear hours or years later, so document the scene, the hazmat information and every change.
slides.sayZh: 这些是你作为 PCP 新要注意的。当 EMR 时，你从不往病人身上扎针；现在可以了，而在受污染的病人身上，静脉通路是一扇新的门，会让化学品绕过皮肤屏障。书中说要尽量减少有创操作、权衡利弊，所以要先完成洗消。BC 规定，呕吐、意识水平下降或收缩压低于九十时不能用 CPAP，而中毒病人常常呕吐或嗜睡。一氧化碳中毒时，要看病人，别看血氧仪。溶剂可能在密闭的救护车里持续释放气体。有些效应要几小时甚至几年后才出现，所以要记录现场情况、危险品信息和每一个变化。

slides.title: Medical monitoring of the entry team
slides.body:
• Before entry: full vitals, temperature, body weight; fluids
  • A Level A suit blocks all four ways to lose heat
  • After (rehab, cold zone): suit off, rest, vitals again
  • Check orientation, fine motor skills, exposure symptoms
  • Weight lost = fluid lost; high temp → watch for heat stroke
  • Abnormal? No re-entry until back to normal

Ask for each member's baseline file. Record agent, PPE, decon type, findings.
slides.say: Hazmat teams may ask you to monitor their entry crew, and your PCP assessment skills shine here. Before they suit up, record full vital signs, temperature and body weight, and have them drink water or a sports drink. A Level A suit blocks all four ways to lose heat, so heat stress adds to the chemical risk. Ask for each member's baseline health file. After technical decon, recheck them in the cold-zone rehab area: suits off, rest, vital signs, orientation to time, place and events, fine motor skills, and exposure symptoms. Weight lost means fluid lost; a high temperature means watch for heat stroke. Anyone abnormal stays out until back to normal.
slides.sayZh: 危险品队可能请你监测进入队员，这正是你 PCP 评估功夫派上用场的地方。他们穿防护服之前，记录完整的生命体征、体温和体重，并让他们喝水或运动饮料。A 级防护服会挡住全部四种散热途径，所以化学品之外还要加上热应激的风险。向队伍要每位队员的基线健康档案。技术洗消之后，在冷区的康复区再查一次：脱下防护服、休息，测生命体征，查对时间、地点和事件的定向力、精细动作，以及有无暴露症状。体重减少就是体液丢失；体温高就要警惕热射病。任何指标异常的人，恢复正常之前都不能再进去。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Not on the BC exam: atropine, pralidoxime, or IO access
  • Not BC exam drugs: hydroxocobalamin, nitrites, thiosulfate
  • Also not exam drugs: calcium for hydrofluoric acid, diuretics
  • CO or smoke: non-rebreather, high-flow O₂
  • Toxic lungs: CHF/Pulmonary Edema protocol; CPAP, PEEP = PCP
  • EMR has no IV; the PCP starts one when indicated
slides.say: For the BC exam, know where the book goes beyond what's tested. The book treats pesticide poisoning with atropine and pralidoxime; neither is on the BC licensing exam, and the exam guidelines have no procedure for intraosseous access, though BCEHS PCPs may place IOs after added-scope training. The cyanide antidotes, hydroxocobalamin and the nitrite and thiosulfate kit, are not among the eighteen BC exam drugs, and neither are calcium for hydrofluoric acid or diuretics. What the BC protocols do give you: a non-rebreather with high-flow oxygen for carbon monoxide and smoke, and the CHF or Pulmonary Edema protocol for toxic lungs, where CPAP and PEEP are PCP-only. And an EMR has no IV; the PCP starts one when indicated.
slides.sayZh: BC 考试要知道书里哪些内容超出了执照考试范围。书里用阿托品和解磷定治疗农药中毒，这两种都不在 BC 执照考试范围内，BC 考纲也没有建立骨髓腔通路的流程，不过 BCEHS 的 PCP 经扩展范围（Schedule 1）培训后可以做骨髓腔置管。氰化物解毒剂，也就是羟钴胺，以及亚硝酸盐加硫代硫酸钠那套，不在 BC 的十八种考试药物里，治疗氢氟酸的钙剂和利尿剂也不在。BC 流程真正给你的是：一氧化碳和烟雾吸入用非重复呼吸面罩加高流量氧；中毒性肺损伤用充血性心衰或肺水肿流程，其中 CPAP 和 PEEP 只有 PCP 能用。还有，EMR 没有静脉权限，PCP 在有指征时开静脉。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Stay back: upwind, uphill, isolate, call; ID via UN number, ERG, SDS
  2. Hot = no entry, warm = decon, cold = you; no patient is fully clean
  3. After decon: PCP adds CPAP/PEEP, IV if indicated; antidotes aren't on the exam

Next: Chapter 54, Crime Scene Awareness
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: at a hazmat scene, stay back. Stop upwind and uphill, isolate, deny entry and call for help, then identify the substance from a distance with the UN number, the ERG and the safety data sheet. Two: hot is off limits, warm is for decon, cold is where you work, and no patient is ever completely clean. Three: after decon, use the BC protocols that fit. The PCP adds CPAP or PEEP when the criteria are met, and an IV when indicated and decon is done; the book's antidotes aren't on the BC licensing exam. Next time: Chapter 54, crime scene awareness, our last chapter. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，危险品现场要远离：停在上风、高处，隔离、禁入、呼叫支援，再用 UN 编号、ERG 和安全数据表在远处辨认物质。二，热区进不去，温区做洗消，冷区才是你工作的地方，而且没有病人能被洗得完全干净。三，洗消后按适用的 BC 流程救治：符合标准时 PCP 加用 CPAP 或 PEEP，有指征且洗消完成后才开静脉；书里的解毒剂不在 BC 执照考试范围内。下节课是第五十四章：犯罪现场警觉，也是我们的最后一章。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
